analysis.title: GS US TMT .. drawdown ..
key_insights: NDX closed down 11% on the week, including a roughly 8% slide Thursday and Friday, a bottom 5 week in 20 years. Semis fell 17%, the worst week for Semiconductors since September 2011.
Cross-asset stress: Gold at 18-month lows, Copper falling sharply, and Nasdaq VIX (VXN) at its highest close since COVID. US Financial Conditions are the tightest in more than 2 years.
Tech-heavy indices are oversold (NDX, SOX, Info Tech, S&P 500, R2K). Valuations are at roughly 10-15 year lows, with NDX at 17x fwd P/E and SOX at about 12-13x.

Desk sees conditions for an oversold bounce, but year-end rally optimism has faded. Fundamentals look healthy (firm compute prices, big beat/raise prints from KEYS, NVDA, PANW), yet there is a buyers' strike with some rotational unwind under the hood.

The October positioning/technical pullback ahead of Midterms has morphed into a Semiconductor bear market by definition. Charts suggest cuts are coming but investors do not see that as a near-term catalyst.
NVDA is setting the tone for sentiment: lower 9 of 10 sessions, down 7 weeks in a row (-13% two weeks ago, -21% last week), and $2.7 trillion of market cap shed in 33 days.
Semis are about 23% below their 200-dma, versus roughly 80% above it at one point this Spring. SOX fwd P/E of 12-13x is at 15+ year lows despite a positive revision cycle.
Info Tech relative drawdown vs the S&P 500 is the second largest in 20+ years, behind only 2013 (PC to Smartphone transition).

GIR Hedge Fund VIP basket (GSTHHVIP) lagged the S&P 500 by 14 pp over six months, rivaling its worst underperformance in 20 years. Apple is outperforming the NDX for the first time since the late-2022 AI cycle start.

Asset-light, non-China-exposed growth cyclicals (Live, Payments, Internet) are not trading better. Desk questions MU down about 25% last week, AAPL, NFLX not trading defensively, and META not holding up.

GIR (Eric Sheridan) lists AMZN, UBER and SPCX as particularly compelling risk/rewards. Alexa for Shopping is projected at about $16+bn of 2026 revenue, and the AWS blue-sky case is mid-50s y/y growth in 2027 and 2028 vs guidance of >40%.
Amazon retail margins face near-term ASP headwinds, with revenue per unit down about 220 bps y/y in 3Q26 on mix shift to Everyday Essentials. Long-term upside comes from automation and cost-to-serve.
GIR (Ben Snider) names 3 conditions for an S&P 500 bottom: improved AI earnings confidence, a dovish Fed signal, and a major decline in investor positioning.

GIR Memory team stays constructive on Samsung and Hynix with about 20% shareholder return yields and downside likely priced in. Forward OP estimates and price targets are coming down on AI capex sustainability worries, weak smartphone/PC demand and rising China supply.

Holiday-shortened week: off-quarter earnings from ADI, ADSK, DELL, WDAY, NTNX, HPQ, ZM, HPE, SMTC, then a busy two-week conference stretch from early December (AWS re:Invent and the sellside circuit). US Core PCE is due Wednesday 11/25.
